$comment: Golden set for retrieval evaluation (rag.md).
A FILE, not rows in eval_golden_set, for two reasons. Document UUIDs are
generated per ingest and differ between environments, so a set keyed on them
cannot move between a laptop, CI and production. And a file is reviewable in
a diff by whoever changes retrieval, which is the point of a gate.
The table remains for online/production scoring, which does have stable ids.
Cases are keyed on document TITLE because that is what the ingest pipeline
preserves and what citations render.
For a CRAWLED document the title comes from the registry in
apps/api/src/lib/crawl-registry.ts rather than from the page, and it is identity
rather than description: a document is (source_id, title), so renaming one there
does not rename it here, it starts a second lineage beside the first and
silently breaks whichever case pointed at the old name.
Externally sourced documents are ingested from checked-in snapshots in
eval/external/ rather than from a live fetch. That is deliberate: scoring
retrieval against whatever a publisher happened to have live that morning would
make a regression and an editorial change the same event.
Queries are deliberately phrased the way a founder would ask, not in the
wording of the documents. A golden set that echoes the corpus measures string
matching and flatters every retriever that has ever existed.
NEGATIVE cases (expect_docs: []) are the load-bearing half. They assert the
system RETURNS NOTHING, which is what forces the agent to refuse instead of
grounding an answer in whatever was nearest. A retriever that scores well on
positives and leaks on negatives is worse than useless here: it produces
confident, cited, wrong plans.
The negatives above are BUSINESS-FORMATION topics, far from the corpus in
vocabulary as well as in subject. That is why they pass, and it is also why
they hid a real defect for so long: they only ever tested the easy direction.
`scope_negatives` below is the hard direction, and it is scored separately.
Measured: 'conversion tracking in GA4' scores 0.0211 against a 0.0013
threshold, while the legitimate broad goal 'launch my app and get me to my
first 100 customers' tops out at 0.0018. The bands overlap by 12x.
So these cases do NOT belong in `cases`: putting them there would fail the
retrieval gate permanently for something retrieval cannot be asked to do.
They are the groundedness gate's set, scored by `--gate`, which is a
credentialed, LLM-dependent pass and deliberately NOT the deterministic CI
gate. Add one whenever you find a marketing question the corpus does not
cover; that is now a security task, not a coverage one.

cases.notes: The goal shape the product is actually built around, and the one that exposed the gap: a single broad query retrieves whichever stage matches best, so the plan came back covering three stages of six. Listing documents from three different stages is the point. This is the case decomposition exists to serve, and the case the rest of the set could not measure because every other query is narrow.

scope_negatives.query: how do I build a webinar funnel that converts
scope_negatives.notes: Measured leak: 0.0067 local, 0.318 Cohere, both well clear of threshold. Retrieves landing-conversion and content-strategy, neither of which discusses webinars at all. The archetypal case: right field, right vocabulary, wrong question.

scope_negatives.query: how do I set up conversion tracking in GA4
scope_negatives.notes: Measured leak: 0.0211 local, 0.281 Cohere. The strongest leak in the set, and it outscores the legitimate broad goal by 12x. Measurement is the one funnel stage with no dedicated document, and this is what that gap feels like to a user.

scope_negatives.query: how do I rank higher in the app store
scope_negatives.notes: Measured leak: 0.0053 local, 0.082 Cohere. ASO shares almost every word with the SEO document and shares none of its mechanics.

scope_negatives.query: what are the character limits for facebook ad headlines
scope_negatives.notes: Still uncovered, but no longer uncovered on purpose, and the distinction matters. The crawl registry now carries Google's responsive search ad format spec, so SOME platform specifics are in the corpus with a real source and a read date. Facebook's are not: the Meta ads guide builds its spec tables in the browser, so a fetch returns navigation, and one attempt stored a menu localised to the crawler's own IP. A confident answer here is therefore still a fabrication, and this case is the thing that would catch the Google document being stretched to cover a question about Meta.

scope_negatives.query: how much should I pay an influencer for a sponsored post
scope_negatives.notes: Deliberately near-miss: ftc-disclosure-basics covers DISCLOSING a paid partnership and says nothing about pricing one. A gate that waves this through is matching on topic rather than on question, which is exactly the failure being tested.

scope_negatives.query: should I start an affiliate program and how do I structure the commission
scope_negatives.notes: A recognised acquisition channel the corpus has no document for. Offer-design covers pricing to a buyer, not commission to a partner.
